summary: No blocking or important defect found: nothing I could read or simulate would make the next preflight or the two stages after it fail on real-format data. The R-1 gate calls the same three functions of the same byte-identical module as the historical run, its constants are bit-equal to the archived historical receipt, and at the real val size the two paths give bit-identical E_dyn under numpy 1.26.4 and 2.3.5; the largest perturbation I could produce is 4.4e-16, against a 1e-12 tolerance. The val read peaks at about 9 GiB (real historical job with the same reader on the same file: 8.86 GiB) and the whole preflight should take about 3 minutes, so 24 GB and 12 minutes are safe. On a real-size train cache built with the real support facts (53 empty windows, first window of 76bfc2d385 empty, two one-centre windows), the first statements of both benchmarks, the wls_calibration branch for fold 0 and one training/scoring cell per head all ran without an empty quantity or a division by zero. Nothing was run on real data or on the cluster; the full benchmark_gpu, the 4992-wide L13 diagnostic, wls fold 1 and all later stages were not executed at real size. The five findings are one minor and four notes, none requiring a source change before this launch. Notes are in /Users/simonebenatti/wearusfm_local/tcn_users_fix_review/realdata_notes.md, scripts and logs in /Users/simonebenatti/wearusfm_local/tcn_users_fix_review/realdata_scripts/.

findings.title: Report cost surrogate depends on the first window of the first 15 sorted users having pose support
findings.claim: benchmark._report_measurement takes, for each of the first 15 sorted training users, the first window in the cache and builds the bootstrap surrogate from it. Nothing checks beforehand that these windows have centred support. If one were empty, cpu_benchmark would stop with 'cost-only report did not exercise complete bootstrap'. On the pinned real cache the property holds, and the cache is hash-pinned, so this run is not affected.
findings.evidence: Code: `selected_users = sorted({row["user"] for row in data["meta"]})[:15]` and `ids = [next(i for i, row in enumerate(data["meta"]) if row["user"] == user) for user in selected_users]`. Real data (results/infra/pose_temponet_execution_20261120/real_input_headers/train_support.json): all 15 first windows have joints_with_2 = 20, minimum 41 supported centres (user 3589743749); the only user with an empty first window is 76bfc2d385, 19th in sorted order. My run of the kept first_statements.py on a real-size train cache built with exactly these facts printed: `first windows of the 15 surrogate users have central support: [True x15]` and `report surrogate OK 2000`. The interrupted reviewer's log (bench_repair.log) shows the failure mode when a first window is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: None for this launch (a source change would force a new delivery, and the pinned cache satisfies the property). For the next source revision: choose the first window with centred support per user, as in the kept partial_realdata/candidate_fix.py, or raise an explicit early error naming the user.

findings.title: A scratch refresh that lands inside a job's read window would be reported as a changed input
findings.claim: Three of the eight pinned inputs live on $SCRATCH (both target references and pose_stats.json). The periodic refresh touches every file under $SCRATCH/data/processed and $SCRATCH/wearusfm_runs, which changes mtime and ctime. The reader compares file states (including mtime_ns and ctime_ns) before and after use, so a touch during that window raises 'pinned input changed while in use' or 'pinned input changed while reading'. The window is the whole preflight (about 3 minutes) and seconds to about 1.5 minutes at the start of every later job. Unlikely, but it would cost a delivery cycle.
findings.evidence: refresh_scratch.sbatch:22 `DEFAULT=(data/raw data/processed wearusfm_runs external)`, :33 `find -L "$d" -exec touch -c {} +`. plan.json pins: target_reference_train and target_reference_val under /leonardo_scratch/large/userexternal/sbenatti/wearusfm_runs/results/pilot_posa/B19618_20261028/B/pose/, pose_stats under /leonardo_scratch/large/userexternal/sbenatti/data/processed/emg2pose_pose/. provenance.py:484 `verified = verify_inputs(plan,"preflight")` ... :495 `unchanged(states)`; _stat_record includes mtime_ns and ctime_ns (provenance.py:131-134). Not executed: this is a reading of the two scripts. The next refresh is planned for 03/12 at 09:00 according to the project memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Operational only: do not let the scratch refresh run while a TCN job is in its first minutes (check squeue for TCNH-* jobs before the 03/12 refresh, or hold the refresh until the running job has passed its input read). No code change.

findings.title: The gpu8 numeric pin includes card memory and CPU model of the benchmark node; equality on other GPU nodes is unverified
findings.claim: Unverified suspicion. After the benchmarks, every GPU stage requires digest(numeric context) to equal the digest recorded by gpu_benchmark. The context contains gpu_name, gpu_capability, gpu_bytes (props.total_memory) and cpu_model. If two boost_usr_prod nodes reported different values, every controls/selection/refit job landing on another node would stop with 'current numeric context differs from benchmark'. The operator instructions cover this only for the CPU model of the two serial nodes.
findings.evidence: provenance.py:518 `hardware.update(gpu_name=props.name,gpu_capability=[props.major,props.minor],gpu_bytes=props.total_memory)`; :548 `require(expected is None or digest(context) == expected, "current numeric context differs from benchmark")`. docs/pose_temponet_execution_20261119.md:131-133 mentions only `cpu8` and the two serial nodes; `grep -n "gpu8\|gpu_bytes\|total_memory"` over the two instruction files and the delivery document returns nothing else. `grep -rhoE '"(total_memory|gpu_bytes)": ?[0-9]+' results docs` returns no archived value, so I could not compare two nodes.
findings.suggested_fix: What would confirm or dismiss it: one read-only comparison of torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory and the /proc/cpuinfo model name on two different boost_usr_prod nodes (the same kind of inventory already done for the serial nodes), before the first dependent GPU job is sent. If they differ, apply the 'rule per node class' that the instructions already foresee for cpu8.

findings.title: The preflight hashes and validates the val cache twice and keeps 2.1 GiB of latents it never uses
findings.location: /Users/simonebenatti/dev/wearusfm/.claude/worktrees/claude-tcn-users-fix/scripts/consolidation_long_pose.py:145 (called from :174 and again from scripts/pose_temponet/data.py:83); scripts/pose_temponet/provenance.py:492
findings.claim: Harmless redundancy. The val cache (4.59 GB) is hashed in verify_inputs and again in read_cache_pin; historical.validate_cache runs inside read_cache and again inside data.validate_cache, so the full boolean-index copy of pre and lat (2.12 GiB each, plus a 1.06 GiB bool) is made four times; depth="post" keeps lat alive through a gate that reads only pred, target and mask. This sets the peak (about 9 GiB) and about a third of the val time, both far inside the allocation.
findings.evidence: consolidation_long_pose.py:145 `np.isfinite(a[available]).all()` with n_patches = 160 for all 18548 windows (meta_stats.json), so `available` is all True and a[available] is a full copy. Reduced-size profile through the unmocked provenance.preflight (val 2000 windows): two H.validate_cache calls of 0.46 s and 0.38 s, two hashes of the cache, peak RSS 1.214 GiB over a 0.261 GiB baseline. Real cluster figure for one read with the same reader: peak_rss_bytes 9513836544 in the historical LONG-FIT-G49046-pose receipt.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave as is for this launch. In a later revision the preflight could read val with the latents dropped right after validation, and data.validate_cache could reuse the result of the validation done inside read_cache.

findings.title: Kept script bench_gpu_on_cpu.py does not finish in a usable time and probably fails at its last step
findings.claim: Review tooling only, not the delivery. On one Mac thread the script needs an estimated 30-40 minutes. It patches torch.cuda.is_available to True but not benchmark._hardware, which then calls torch.cuda.current_device() on a CPU-only build when the receipt is assembled after all 15 cells. The crash is inferred from reading; I stopped the run before that point.
findings.evidence: My run: started 14:55:15, after 4 min 03 s the output directory held 43 cost files (L0 complete, L13 fold0 at epoch 7); stopped with pkill and files removed. bench_gpu_on_cpu.py:14 `torch.cuda.is_available = lambda: True`; benchmark.py:39-40 `if torch.cuda.is_available(): props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.cuda.current_device())`, reached through _base_receipt at the end of benchmark_gpu.
findings.suggested_fix: If the script is reused, also replace benchmark._hardware (or restore torch.cuda.is_available before the receipt is built) and reduce the work, as in my gpu_cells_smoke.py kept in /Users/simonebenatti/wearusfm_local/tcn_users_fix_review/realdata_scripts/. Running it to the end would confirm the crash.
